implementation_plan: Stage 0 - reconcile existing partial presentation before writing code. Builder must inspect current main.js first because terrain, wall/gate draw, queue preview, HUD and lightning renderer already exist. Do not duplicate these systems. Treat PI-007 as completing and hardening the missing spawn/clip/ownership pieces.

Stage 1 - draw pipeline hardening in main.js. Preserve outside terrain as full-canvas ground/asphalt. Use a clipped arena block for arena floor plus active gameplay objects: Speed Dot/lightning, onions, player, player bullets and explosions through player.draw(). Draw decorative queued previews outside the arena before the final wall/gate overlay, then draw walls/gates after entities so the arena frame remains readable. Preserve screen shake around all gameplay canvas layers and preserve screen flash after restore. Fallback no-arena branch may keep outside terrain plus un-clipped entities.

Stage 2 - extract gate geometry to one pure helper. Add js/core/ArenaGates.js with resolveArenaGates(arena) and resolveGateSpawn(arena,radius,spawnIndex,rng) or equivalent small API. The helper reads arena.points and arena.normals only; it must not mutate Arena or store runtime state. Replace main.js local getArenaGates() with the helper import. Keep drawWallRun(), drawGate(), drawArenaWallsAndGates() and queued preview drawing in main.js for now; do not create a rendering subsystem.

Stage 3 - gate-based onion spawn in LevelManager.js. Import the gate helper and replace only the random edge position block inside #spawnQueuedOnion(). Use spawnIndex = waveState.spawnedOnions before entity creation. Select a gate by spawnIndex modulo gates.length, with small tangent jitter inside gate.length/2 minus onion radius. Place the onion at gate center + inward normal * (radius + small margin), then call arena.constrainCircle() exactly as today. If no arena/gates are available, retain the current random-edge fallback. Increment spawnedOnions only after the onion is pushed, exactly as today.

Stage 4 - queued onion preview compatibility in main.js. Keep preview decorative, outside the arena, and derived from levelManager.getWaveProgress().queuedOnions. Use the same helper gate ordering as spawn so preview location and spawn language match. Cap preview drawing only if visual tests show clutter; any cap must be visual-only and must not alter queuedOnions semantics or HUD count.

Stage 5 - right HUD check, not redesign. Existing DOM and updateRunHud() already expose queued, boost and bolt state. Build should only adjust labels, CSS sizing or text fallback if visual verification finds overlap on desktop or <=900px layouts. HUD remains pointer-events none and read-only over LevelManager/player state.

Stage 6 - continuous transition regression check. Do not change the normal wave completion branch except if the draw/spawn changes require a narrow updateRunHud() placement. Explicitly verify no call to showLevelOverlay(), engine.stop() or fadeBgm(0,800) is reintroduced in the wave-completion path.

Stage 7 - speed/lightning compatibility check. Keep current Speed Dot API names for backward compatibility. Keep drawSpeedDot() visual as lightning/bolt. Do not touch Player.js or Onion.js unless the build finds that existing proportional boost rings are unreadable after terrain/wall changes; if touched, limit to visual ring readability and do not change boost timing, multiplier, no-stack or pickup semantics.
